recommendations.section: ## 2. Training Topologies on a No-P2P PCIe Fabric
recommendations.current: Six ways to split a training job across five cards, and they differ in what their communication scales with. Data parallelism (DDP) replicates the model and all-reduces gradients once per optimizer step, so its traffic scales with parameter count and not with sequence length. Fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP, also called ZeRO-3) shards parameters, gradients and optimizer state, all-gathering each layer before use and reduce-scattering it after — the same parameter scaling, paid per layer. Pipeline parallelism (PP) splits the model by layer into stages and passes activations between them, so its traffic scales with tokens × hidden × stages. Tensor parallelism (TP) splits each layer's matrices across ranks and all-reduces inside every layer, so its traffic scales with tokens × hidden × layers and sits on the critical path. Expert parallelism (EP) distributes mixture-of-experts (MoE) experts across ranks and all-to-alls each token's activations to the ranks holding its experts. Sequence parallelism (SP) shards the sequence dimension across ranks and exchanges attention state per layer — Ulysses by all-to-all on the head dimension, Ring Attention by P2P ring passes of K/V blocks — and at 32k it is the standard alternative to activation checkpointing.
recommendations.recommended:

recommendations.section: ## 6. CSA2 Sparse Attention at 32k Context
recommendations.current:
The plan cites NSA's 6.3× forward and 3.4× backward at 32k as evidence of a large sparse-attention win. Those are kernel-level ratios measured on 8×A100 with Triton kernels [[native-sparse-attention-hardware-aligned-and-natively]] (T3).

FSA (ICLR 2026) is the measured end-to-end comparison the corpus needed: Llama3-8B, Qwen3-14B and Qwen2.5-32B at 32K and 64K in BF16, on H20 and H200 with NVLink. It reports up to 1.25× and 1.09× on average end-to-end training speedup over the Triton NSA kernel, and up to 2.47× and 1.86× on average over full attention [[published-as-a-conference-paper-at-iclr-2026]] (T3). Dividing the two averages implies NSA ≈ 1.71× full attention end-to-end, not 6.3×. The fla-org Triton implementation reproduces a shrinking advantage: 2.66× forward at 16,384 tokens, 1.35× at 8,192, and 0.72× at 4,096 — NSA is slower than flash at short context [[github-fla-orgnative-sparse-attention-efficient-triton-implementations-for-nativ]] (T2).

recommendations.section: ## 4. MoE and Expert Parallelism: Ruled Out or Misjudged?
recommendations.current:
The plan's estimate — two all-to-alls per MoE layer, ~70× the compute time at 1M-token batches — divides the aggregate dispatch-plus-combine volume across all ranks (~400 GB) by the per-GPU collective rate. Each GPU sends only its share.

Megatron-Core's per-GPU send volume in one all-to-all is T·K·h·(EP−1)/EP, where T is the tokens on that GPU, K is top-k, h is hidden width and EP is the expert-parallel size [[scalable-training-of-mixture-of-experts-models-with]] (T3). At a 1M-token global batch over five data-parallel ranks, T_local = 200,000; with top-k 2, hidden 2048 and EP=5, dispatch is 200,000 × 2 × 2048 × 0.8 = 6.55 × 10⁸ elements = 1.31 GB in bf16; dispatch plus combine is 2.62 GB per layer; across 24 MoE layers that is 62.9 GB per GPU per step (T4). At 0.805 GB/s that is 78 s, or 1.39× the corrected 56.3 s window.
